before.description: Same city, new metabolism: harvest A7 + B7

reading.text: The living partners remain installed, but repair now takes three units. Total harvest is 14 instead of 17; the earlier 10/7 promise cannot simply continue. The changed city retains its infrastructure and its recorded allocation problem.
reading.attribution: Explicit speculative fiction, not an existing capability or a biological construction protocol.

after.label: Same city, new metabolism: harvest A7 + B7
after.description: Same city, new metabolism: harvest A7 + B7

reading.text: The installed partner now diverts three units to repair: A’s harvest falls from 10 to 7, while B remains at 7. Total harvest is 14 rather than 17. A’s adopted 5-day/5-night allocation now promises 3 more units than its harvest, on top of its already recorded night shortfall of 1. The same city retains its living partners and current winter agreement; the old 6/6 trial cannot supply the missing food.
reading.attribution: Explicit speculative fiction, not an existing capability or a biological construction protocol.

after.label: Raw clock 31° W; Moon 30°30′ W ±35′
after.description: The centres differ by 30 arcminutes, but the raw clock centre remains inside the lunar range.

reading.text: The raw clock worksheet gives 31° W: 14:06 mean − 2 minutes = 14:04 apparent, compared with local 12:00. The lunar worksheet gives 30°30′ W ±35′, a band of 29°55′–31°05′ W. Their centres differ by 30′, yet 31° W lies inside that lunar band. This comparison alone neither proves the clock wrong nor measures its gain. The independently recorded voyage rate, not the Moon, supplies the clock correction. Both worksheets use the same local-noon observation.
reading.attribution: Fictional voyage day 20, in an imagined 1768 voyage. All sights share one instant on day 20. Modern midnight-based 00–24-hour notation is used; values are invented, not an ephemeris for a real calendar date or usable navigation data.

before.label: Living city: repair continues; harvest shared 7 and 7
before.description: Living city: repair continues; harvest shared 7 and 7

reading.text: The observatory checks the new balance rather than blaming the old day/night schedule. The city keeps the partner’s repair running and activates the agreed equal-share fallback: 14 available units, seven for each district. A changes to 3 by day and 4 at night; B likewise receives seven. Output has not magically returned to 17. The living city survives as an institution that can alter its operation when its biology changes, with a real scarcity still to investigate.
reading.attribution: Explicit speculative fiction, not an existing capability or a biological construction protocol.

after.label: Living city: A3+4, B7; repair continues, night 2 short
after.description: Living city: repair continues; harvest shared 7 and 7

reading.text: The city applies the current winter agreement’s biological-change fallback, not the obsolete 6/6 trial. The partner’s repair continues; the 14 available units are shared 7 and 7. A receives 3 by day and 4 at night: its night need remains 6, explicitly short by 2. B receives 7. Output has not magically returned to 17. The same living installation changes its allocation without pretending the remaining shortage is solved; that unmet need remains visible for the next collective revision.
reading.attribution: Explicit speculative fiction, not an existing capability or a biological construction protocol.

before.label: Merchant manual
before.description: The worked example and general reasoning serve a second account rather than requiring a new memorized answer.

after.label: Unit-rate manual: divide, then scale
after.description: The worked example and general reasoning serve a second account rather than requiring a new memorized answer.

reading.text: Three equal cloth lengths cost 18 units: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 units per length; five lengths cost 5 × 6 = 30. The general calculation keeps the quantities and their units together: total amount ÷ number of equal units gives an amount per unit; multiply that rate by the new number of units. This is the worked merchant example joined to the earlier general algebraic method, not a new memorized answer.
reading.attribution: Authored merchant-arithmetic worksheet, not a quotation from Fibonacci. Reuse in later calculations is a pedagogical connection, not a claim that this particular manual was transmitted.

before.label: Winter commons: folded wall; A5+5, B7
before.description: The living infrastructure and the shared rule operate as one revisable system; neither engineering nor governance is an afterthought.

reading.text: The same living installation adopts the winter position and allocation. A distributes 5 in daylight and stores 5 for night; B receives the restored-light harvest of 7. Governance has changed the actual panel position and food schedule, not merely certified the machine.
reading.attribution: Explicit speculative fiction, not an existing capability or a biological construction protocol.

after.label: Winter commons: A5+5, B7; night shortfall 1
after.description: The living infrastructure and the shared rule operate as one revisable system; neither engineering nor governance is an afterthought.

reading.text: The same living installation folds the wall and applies the adopted winter agreement. A distributes 5 in daylight and stores 5 for night; its night need remains 6, so 1 is unmet. B receives its restored-light harvest of 7. The visible shortage is the accepted cost of this allocation, not erased by the higher regional total. Governance has changed the actual panel position and schedule while recording whose need remains unmet.
reading.attribution: Explicit speculative fiction, not an existing capability or a biological construction protocol.

before.label: Predictive sky record
before.description: Old recurrence and newer positional models can both be checked against records; a stronger model must still answer inherited observations.

after.label: Sky record: dated positions and predicted changes
after.description: Old recurrence and newer positional models can both be checked against records; a stronger model must still answer inherited observations.

reading.text: The worksheet keeps an observed date and position beside the model’s predicted position, retaining their discrepancy. Older recurrence records and newer positional tables remain comparable records, not interchangeable guarantees. A pair of predicted positions at known times also supplies a change in position over a time interval. A stated straight-line interpolation rule can turn that interval into a rate and estimate an intermediate time; the approximation belongs to the interval, not to all celestial motion.
reading.attribution: Authored astronomical-table method, not a quotation or numerical transcription from Tycho or Kepler. Its later reuse is pedagogical; it does not claim that Kepler invented interpolation.

before.label: Revisable agreement
before.description: Users have a way to contest and alter the rule; revision is part of the institution rather than evidence of total failure.

after.label: Agreement: affected users can challenge and revise allocations
after.description: Users have a way to contest and alter the rule; revision is part of the institution rather than evidence of total failure.

reading.text: The downstream shortfall remains in the record beside the original allocation. Affected users can inspect the observations, challenge whose needs the allocation meets, and change the rule through their agreed review process. The revision preserves the stated needs and the remaining shortfalls; renaming the agreement cannot turn insufficient resources into sufficient resources.
reading.attribution: Authored commons case informed by Ostrom, not a quotation, legal instrument, or universal allocation rule.

before.label: Winter: fold the wall; A10 and B7, review each season
before.description: A proposed rule changes production and shading across seasons. Those affected can revise it as their experience and the ecology change.

reading.text: The agreed winter configuration folds the productive surface. A accepts a reduction from 12 to 10 while B rises from 4 to 7. Distribution is rescheduled within A’s smaller harvest, 5 by day and 5 at night. The agreement also specifies an equal-share fallback if a biological change makes the total inadequate; it is a revisable fictional arrangement, not a universal rule.
reading.attribution: Explicit speculative fiction, not an existing capability or a biological construction protocol.

after.label: Winter agreement: A5+5, B7; A’s night is 1 short
after.description: A proposed rule changes production and shading across seasons. Those affected can revise it as their experience and the ecology change.

reading.text: The agreed winter configuration folds the surface: A’s harvest falls from 12 to 10 while B rises from 4 to 7. A chooses 5 by day and 5 at night, explicitly accepting a night shortfall of 1 against the stated need of 6. This is a negotiated ration, not a claim that every need is met. The agreement keeps the need visible for seasonal review. If biological repair reduces the available total to 14, its fallback keeps repair running and gives 7 to each district; A then receives 3 by day and 4 at night, explicitly 2 short of its night need. This is a revisable fictional arrangement, not a universal allocation rule.
reading.attribution: Explicit speculative fiction, not an existing capability or a biological construction protocol.

after.description: The sheet keeps the whole calculation: 14:06 mean − 2 minutes for apparent time − 2 minutes gained = 14:02 apparent reference time. Against local 12:00, that is 122 minutes × 15′ = 30°30′ W; equivalently subtract 30′ from the raw 31° W. Worst-case time bound combines ±20 seconds of clock residual and ±20 seconds of local noon: ±40 seconds, equivalent to ±10′ of longitude. Clock band: 30°20′–30°40′ W.
